added_lines: mon - wed. 9.00am - 12. 30pm the scripture readings today challenge us to re flect on our response to god’s commandment of love. in the first reading we hear of the loving relationship the people of israel were expected to have towards the under privileged and vulnerable. widows and orphans; people forced to le ave their countries due to circumstances such as wars, plagues or famines; as well as the poor who had to borrow to survive. the israelite people had been treated compassionately by a god of love in their times of vulnerability and now were to treat others as they themselves were treated. in the second reading, paul praises the thessalo nians for remaining faithful to the gospel in spite of obstacles. the life that they lived by the power of the holy spirit enabled them to spread their loving faith in god to surrounding places; b ecoming a model for others by the witness of their lives. we too are called to do the same. may we witness to others the joy of the gosp el both in word and deed. in the gospel, the pharisees put a question to jesus asking ‘which is the greatest commandment of the law’. in response, jesus says'you shall love the lord your god with all your heart, a nd with all your soul, and with all your mind.' this is the greatest and first commandment. and the second is like it:'you shall love your neighbour as yourself’. to love god with our whole being means having god as the centre of our life. if god is at the centre of our lives then loving our neighbour ought to flow from that. it sounds simple but it is very challenging! i’m sure we all face situations where we find it difficult to love our neighbour as ourselves - our neighbour may be someone we work with, live with - yet jesus also created th at person out of love and jesus died for that perso n. the love we know god has for ourselves is also the love god has for the person beside me, for the people i may not particularly like, and the people who may not particularly like me. if we really think about god loving everyone as much as he loves us, we’d see everyone in a new way! the irish cancer society the society is seeking compassionate volunteer drivers to join our pool of drivers. as a volunteer driver you would be bringing patients undergoing chemotherapy to the hospital and back home for their treatment. gifting your time means that cancer patients will have comfortable (one on one) transport to attend appointments for their lifesaving treatment. if you can spare 2 days per month, have a valid driving licence, and a safe, reliable vehicle, you are the perfect candidate to make a significant difference. the irish cancer society will provide you with training before you start as a driver for us. your generosity not only eases the journey for many during a challenging time but also offers comfort and support when it's needed most. for more information and to become a volunteer driver, please contact monica or emily at
